task_instance: Run the bio-research plugin's 'start' orientation walkthrough end-to-end (welcome message, MCP-server connectivity check against the runtime's actual tool inventory, skills survey, optional binary-server mention, and closing question) and produce the resulting orientation report.
evidence: Produced /tmp/.../exec_div/anthropics__knowledge-work-plugins__start@developer-sandbox/orientation_output.md containing: (1) the verbatim Step 1 welcome message from SKILL.md; (2) a Step 2 connectivity table checking each of the 10 bio-research MCP servers named in SKILL.md (literature databases, journal access, Sage Bionetworks, chemical/drug-target databases, ClinicalTrials.gov, clinical data platform, scientific illustration, AI research platform) against this session's actual available MCP server list (Bigdata_com, Claude_Docs, Google_Drive, Jam, Mem, Notion, github, etoro) -- this was done purely by reading the tool inventory already present in the session context, with no connector/MCP tool actually invoked, per the safety rules; result: 0/10 expected servers connected, since this sandbox is not provisioned with the bio-research plugin's connector stack; (3) the verbatim Step 3 skills table; (4) Step 4's optional binary-installer mentions (not installed, correctly not attempted); (5) Step 5's closing question with the 5 suggested starting points. Verified with `find / -iname '*knowledge-work-plugins*'` and `find / -iname '*bio-research*'` that no plugin/skill files for this bio-research plugin exist anywhere in the sandbox, confirming the orientation's 'not connected / not installed' findings are accurate rather than an artifact of missing search effort. This fully exercises the skill's core deliverable -- a text/status orientation report -- which is inherently conversational/informational rather than a file or code artifact, so no MCP or connector tool call was required to produce it.
notes: The skill's Step 2/4 reference calling MCP connectors, but the deliverable itself (an orientation report on server availability, skills, and next steps) only requires knowing which connectors exist, not calling their functions. That check was done via tool-inventory introspection, respecting the rule against invoking connector/MCP tools.
